newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Wednesday, with an active domestic A share market attracting funds from the repo market, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 12.50 percent from 11.80 percent on Tuesday.
Turnover rose to 6.56 million lots from 5.01 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said institutions borrowed money on the repo market to speculate in the A share market, which is expected to be on a upward trend in the short term.
An A share issue by Eastern Communications Co on Thursday in particular pushed up early-maturing contracts, they said.
Traders believe the trend to continue in the next few days.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended down in dull trading, with sentiment very weak on continued falls.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, fell to 121.60 yuan from 122.30 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market increased to 1.05 million lots from 993,547 lots.
Traders expect contracts to remain weak in the short term. -- Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
